implementation_notes: Rust fights this shape hard, which is why the support level is discouraged. A god object must be constructed once and then borrowable everywhere, so its methods take `&mut self` and every caller that touches two responsibilities hits a borrow conflict, or reaches for `Arc<Mutex<Self>>` and trades the compile errors for runtime lock contention. The idiomatic counter is free functions and traits: `impl Invoice { fn total(&self) -> Money }` on the type that owns the fields, `&dyn Repository` at the seams, and `#[non_exhaustive]` so adding a variant is not a breaking change. A `pub struct App { /* everything */ }` re-exported from `lib.rs` and passed to every function is the god object in Rust clothing, and `cargo` will not stop it.
idiom_name: single `App`/`Context` struct with one giant `impl` block
alternative: Split the state into owned domain types, make each function take `&self` on the narrow type it needs, and pass collaborators as `&dyn Trait`; keep no struct in the project that both holds the domain state and exposes the operations of more than one responsibility.
pitfalls: `Arc<Mutex<App>>` converts a compile-time god object into a runtime one: now every caller serialises on one lock and deadlocks become possible.
`#[non_exhaustive]` on a god enum silences the match-exhaustiveness error that would otherwise have revealed the variant explosion.
`Default` derive on the god struct makes the 'what does this depend on' question unanswerable from the type alone.
